title: Buckaroo Bowl II
dek: Kaushal's Habibsters routed Ramon's Araleasers 261.44 to 145.28 over NFL weeks 17 and 18 of the 2024 season, winning by 116.2 points to become the first repeat champion in Buckaroo Football League history.
body: Buckaroo Bowl II was the championship of the 2024 Buckaroo Football League season, the league's second year and its second with six teams. Like every Bowl, it was scored as a two-week total, played across NFL weeks 17 and 18. It matched the top-seeded Habibsters, managed by Kaushal, against the third-seeded Araleasers, managed by Ramon.

The Habibsters entered as defending champions, having won Buckaroo Bowl I in 2023. Habib's team went 11-3 in the 2024 regular season and scored 1,524.8 points, about 108.9 a week. Luffy made them overwhelming favorites, giving them a 93 percent chance to win the title before kickoff.

The Araleasers took a more winding path. Brucie's team finished the regular season 7-7 with 1,430.9 points, about 102.2 a week, and arrived at the final with no earlier titles and a 7 percent title chance from Luffy. For a manager who had not been sure he even wanted to join the league, reaching the Bowl in his second season was a significant result in itself.

The teams met three times in the 2024 regular season. The Araleasers won the first meeting in week 2, 112.46 to 102.24, but the Habibsters took the next two decisively: 122.26 to 69.42 in week 7 and 111.76 to 56.4 in week 12. Buckaroo Bowl II was the first playoff meeting between the two managers.

The Habibsters reached the final by beating Alan's Team Pillbert 296.96 to 245.08 in the two-week semifinal over weeks 15 and 16. Rookie receiver Brian Thomas Jr. led them with 51.2 points, and the 296.96 total showed a lineup peaking at the right time. Philly's 245.08 would have won plenty of playoff rounds; it simply ran into the defending champion.

The Araleasers advanced past Randy's The fumblers, 202.44 to 176.14, in the other semifinal. Quarterback Josh Allen carried them with 52.4 points across the two weeks. Their winning total was nearly 95 points lower than the Habibsters' semifinal score, a gap that pointed toward the final's outcome.

Week 17 opened with Patrick Mahomes, who threw two first-quarter touchdown passes for the Habibsters in Kansas City's game at Pittsburgh, to Xavier Worthy from 7 yards and Justin Watson from 11. The Araleasers answered through Josh Allen, who ran in a 1-yard touchdown in the first quarter against the Jets, and Mike Evans, who caught touchdown passes of 2 and 1 yards from Baker Mayfield in the first half against Carolina. Mahomes's third touchdown pass, a 12-yarder to Travis Kelce in the fourth quarter, counted for both sides, since Kelce was in Ramon's lineup.

The rest of the week tilted toward the Habibsters. Allen added third-quarter touchdown passes to Amari Cooper and Keon Coleman, and Bijan Robinson scored on two 1-yard runs in the first half at Washington, but Kaushal's lineup kept answering. Jake Elliott kicked field goals of 31 and 26 yards, Sam LaPorta caught a 6-yard touchdown with a two-point conversion against San Francisco, and Brian Thomas Jr. scored on an 11-yard catch in the fourth quarter at Jacksonville. Jahmyr Gibbs closed the week with a 30-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter at San Francisco. The Habibsters led 138.8 to 87.5 after week 17, a 51.3-point cushion.

Week 18 turned the lead into a rout. Robinson again scored twice for the Araleasers, on runs of 3 and 4 yards against Carolina, and Elliott added field goals of 24 and 32 yards for the Habibsters against the Giants. Ladd McConkey added a two-point conversion catch at Las Vegas. The Araleasers scored 57.8 points for the week, and only four of their starters (Robinson, Evans, the Cowboys D/ST and Jayden Reed) put up anything at all.

Gibbs then supplied the signature performance of the Bowl in Detroit's home finale against Minnesota. He scored on a 25-yard run in the first quarter, a 10-yard catch from Jared Goff in the third, and runs of 13 and 4 yards in the fourth, four touchdowns in a game the championship no longer needed. The Habibsters won week 18 122.6 to 57.8 and the Bowl 261.44 to 145.28. The 116.2-point margin was larger than anything the Araleasers scored in either week.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the game's standout. He scored 67.8 points across the two weeks against a projection of 42.2: 24.3 in week 17 and 43.5 in week 18, with five total touchdowns. He had averaged 17.9 points a start for the Habibsters before the final, and he nearly doubled that rate when it mattered most.

Ladd McConkey was the biggest surprise. He scored 39.4 points against a 23.9 projection, after just 26 points in three earlier starts for the team (8.7 a start), including 25.4 in week 17 alone. Brian Thomas Jr. continued his playoff form with 34.2 points against a 31.2 projection. Mahomes scored 26 against a 17.5 projection, all of it in week 17. LaPorta added 25.2 against a 19.4 projection, after managing just 13.4 points in three earlier starts for Kaushal.

Not everything worked for the champions. Justin Jefferson scored 20.1 points against a 36-point projection, well under his 16.3-a-start pace across two weeks. In week 18, Sam Darnold scored 7.6 points at quarterback against a 20.6 projection, and the Chiefs D/ST finished at minus 8 for the week. Those misses barely registered against the size of the lead.

For the Araleasers, Bijan Robinson did everything he could, scoring 53.6 points against a 38.6 projection with four rushing touchdowns, two in each week. Mike Evans added 39.1 against a 26.8 projection, and Kelce scored 18.4 against a 10.5 projection, all in week 17. Josh Allen, Ramon's semifinal hero, scored 23 points against a 28-point projection, all of it in week 17. Jayden Reed scored 5.2 points against a 20-point projection, and the Cowboys D/ST scored 6, including minus 4 in week 17.

The Araleasers' lineup carried three starters who scored nothing across both weeks. Running backs Alvin Kamara and David Montgomery were each projected for 0 points and scored 0, and kicker Greg Zuerlein scored 0 against a 7.1 projection. Starting two running backs projected for zero in a championship was the kind of choice the league does not let go of easily.

Meanwhile, the Araleasers' bench outscored much of the starting lineup. DeVonta Smith scored 27 points, all in week 17, against a 10.9 projection. Najee Harris added 22.7, Calvin Ridley 20.4, James Cook 20.1, Jordan Love 16.8, Kyle Pitts 14.9 and Brandon Aubrey 14. In all, the bench produced 139.3 points, only about six fewer than the 145.28 that counted.

Better choices would not have changed the result. Putting Harris and Cook in for Kamara and Montgomery, Smith in for Reed, and Aubrey in for Zuerlein would have added roughly 79 points, still well short of the 116.2-point margin. On the Habibsters' side, Bucky Irving's 15.4 bench points in week 18 were a luxury the champions never needed.

The win made Kaushal the league's first repeat champion and, after two seasons, its only champion, following his victory in Buckaroo Bowl I. The Habibsters finished first of six for the second straight year. Their 261.44 points and the 116.2-point margin made Buckaroo Bowl II the most one-sided showcase yet of the league's early dynasty. At the other end of the 2024 table, Sonny's Ben Dover finished last for the second straight season, keeping the consolation ladder's shame in familiar hands.

The Araleasers finished second of six, a strong showing for a 7-7 team that entered with a 7 percent title chance. The ending was less kind. In 2025 Ramon ran the Araleasers through week 8 before being removed from the league for inactivity. The team, renamed Ramon's Remains, played out the season without him and promptly went on a winning streak. Brucie returned for the 2026 expansion season with No Banner only HULK.

The Habibsters' run ended in 2025, when Sonny completed a worst-to-first turnaround with Ben Dover, going 13-3 and winning Buckaroo Bowl III. Habib's two titles in the league's first two seasons remained the benchmark the rest of the league was chasing heading into the eight-team era.
